items.title: SBI launches CyRIS centre to strengthen cybersecurity capabilities
items.description: SBI proudly introduces CyRIS, its new Cybersecurity Centre of Excellence, designed to elevate digital protection and competence. This centre will delve into vital aspects like threat intelligence, cyber defense mechanisms, and ethical hacking practices. It also emphasizes malware analysis, AI security, and quantum-safe advances, showcasing SBI's unwavering resolve to fortify cybersecurity across the financial landscape through collaborative efforts.

items.title: NBFCs curb fresh loans in rural markets as weak monsoon raises repayment risks
items.description: India's leading non-bank lenders like Shriram Finance and Bajaj Finance are limiting new lending in drought-affected regions. The lenders are closely monitoring borrowers for early signs of repayment difficulties due to weak monsoon rainfall. Companies are adjusting loan growth expectations downward and strengthening collection efforts in impacted locations. Several states are under close scrutiny as economic pressures mount from lower incomes and agricultural yields.

items.title: D-St set for a negative opening as GIFT Nifty signals weak start
items.description: Benchmark Nifty gained on Monday, while broader markets also rallied amid ongoing geopolitical tensions. Analysts suggest that Indian stock markets will trade sideways until there is greater clarity on global developments. Foreign portfolio investors net sold shares, while domestic institutional investors were net buyers. The rupee depreciated for the third consecutive day, influenced by elevated crude oil prices.

items.title: Stocks in news: Paytm, Tata Consumer, Dalmia Bharat, REC and DCM Shriram
items.description: Indian equity markets showed recovery with a rise in NSE Nifty 50, ending a four-session losing streak. Several companies reported their September-quarter earnings, highlighting varying financial performances. Paytm experienced significant profit growth, while Dalmia Bharat reported a net loss due to an exceptional charge. Defence stocks are also in focus following government procurement approvals. Investors continue to track earnings reports and related developments in the market.

items.title: Jio IPO delivers smaller payday for bankers than other mega offerings
items.description: In a landmark move, Jio Platforms, supported by Mukesh Ambani, successfully secured ₹30,213 crore, marking the largest IPO in India’s history. Investment bankers were rewarded with ₹196 crore in fees, translating to only 0.65% of the total amount raised. In contrast, Hyundai Motor India achieved ₹27,859 crore while paying out a heftier ₹493 crore in fees, which amount to 1.77%.

items.title: Indian markets rebound, but rising oil prices keep investors cautious
items.description: On Monday, Indian equity markets staged a comeback following four days of losses, with both the BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty seeing notable gains as investors sought to take advantage of cheaper stock prices. However, analysts warn that this recovery is precarious, influenced by global geopolitical issues and high crude oil prices.

items.title: Retail investors return to equities with Rs 10,572 crore buying in September
items.description: After two months of silence, September marked the return of retail investors to the secondary market, as they invested ₹10,572 crore in equities. This shift occurred after a significant market dip linked to escalating oil prices. In contrast, foreign portfolio investors continued their exit strategy. Additionally, the primary market thrived with ₹5,650 crore in shares bought by retail investors, emphasizing that upcoming market conditions will shape their future involvement.

items.title: Rising concentration in AI stocks poses a risk: Kunal Kapoor, Morningstar CEO
items.description: Kunal Kapoor, the CEO of Morningstar, voiced unease about the dangers of focusing investments heavily on AI stocks during his Mumbai trip. He stressed that lofty expectations might not always reflect in company profits, potentially leading to disappointing market outcomes. While praising India's compelling growth story, he remarked that its investment valuations do not stand up favorably against those in emerging markets.

items.title: India earns nearly 50% more from fuel exports in April-September as costlier oil and weak rupee outweigh lower volumes
items.description: India's petroleum product export earnings increased significantly in April to September, driven by high international prices. While the volume of shipments declined by 16%, earnings surged by nearly 50% in rupee terms. Diesel exports were the largest contributors to the earnings growth, accounting for 42% of the total volume. Both diesel and petrol consumption rose during this period, whereas production saw slight declines.

items.title: Govt seeks investor and expert views on LTCG and STT as it reviews capital market levies amid FPI exodus
items.description: The government has initiated a reassessment of long-term capital gains tax and securities transaction tax. Stakeholders, including investors and tax experts, have been consulted for their views. The debate has gained momentum due to significant outflows of foreign portfolio investments. Current taxation methods may affect the attractiveness of Indian equities compared to global markets. The upcoming budget provides an opportunity to revisit these tax regulations.

items.title: Noel Tata renews challenge to Chandrasekaran’s reappointment, questions Tata Sons board voting and conflict of interest
items.description: Noel Tata has raised concerns about N Chandrasekaran's reappointment as executive chairman of Tata Sons. His objections relate to board procedures, including voting requirements and potential conflicts of interest. The board approved Chandrasekaran's position despite Noel Tata's requests for detailed meeting records. Additionally, he questioned the legitimacy of the meeting agenda and the absence of a selection committee.

items.title: Stock Radar: Cyient stock hits fresh 52-week high after nearly 2-month consolidation; is it time to buy?
items.description: Cyient Ltd has recently broken out of a consolidation phase, hitting a fresh 52-week high. The stock demonstrates bullish momentum, with short-term targets above 1,300 levels in a few weeks. Analysts suggest that the price structure indicates a continuation of the upward trend. Immediate obstacles have been cleared, paving the way for further gains ahead. Investors are advised to consider strategic entries and protect capital with stop-loss measures.

items.title: Jio Platforms shares to list on BSE, NSE tomorrow;  GMP signals 22% premium
items.description: Jio Platforms shares are set to list on the BSE and NSE on October 28, with the IPO commanding a grey market premium of around 22%. The Rs 30,213-crore issue was subscribed 22.19 times, led by strong institutional demand. Investors will watch the listing amid Jio’s growth ambitions and financial performance.

items.title: TCS, Infosys, other IT stocks drop up to 3% as Anthropic IPO sparks rally in global AI stocks
items.description: Indian IT stocks fell amid reports that Anthropic, the maker of Claude, is preparing for an IPO that could value it at around $1.5 trillion. While the listing would open up investment opportunities in a leading AI developer, rising infrastructure costs, mounting losses and concerns over growth sustainability remain key risks.

items.title: Mankind Pharma among 5 F&O stocks with a sharp rise in futures open interest
items.description: As of October 26, five stocks in the NSE F&O segment recorded a rise of more than 7% in futures open interest compared with the previous trading session, according to StockEdge F&O scan data. A notable increase in futures open interest indicates a substantial rise in the number of active, unexpired futures contracts in a security. This may reflect market participants initiating new positions or increasing the size of their existing positions.

items.title: Sona BLW Precision Forgings shares rally 6% after Q2 profit rises 29%, revenue jumps 35%
items.description: Sona Comstar shares surged nearly 6% after the company reported record Q2FY27 revenue and profit, driven by robust growth in its electric-vehicle business, new orders and product launches.

items.title: Sigma Advanced Systems shares rally 5% after securing Rs 973 crore NATO order
items.description: Sigma Advanced Systems shares rallied after the defence manufacturer secured a Rs 973-crore order from a NATO customer for Base Bleed Units used in 155 mm artillery ammunition. The contract strengthens its push towards vertical integration and expanded manufacturing capabilities.

items.title: Ather Energy shares jump 5%, extend rally to 20% in two days after Q2 results. Can the run continue?
items.description: Ather Energy shares extended their rally on Tuesday after the electric two-wheeler maker reported its first quarterly profit of Rs 1.26 crore in Q2 FY27. Revenue surged 63% year-on-year to Rs 1,464 crore, while EBITDA turned positive. Nomura raised its target price to Rs 2,070 and retained its Buy rating.

items.title: Sensex, Nifty extend gains despite oil hovering near $115/barrel. What lies ahead?
items.description: The Indian stock market nudged upward on Tuesday, with Sensex and Nifty making modest gains despite lingering challenges. Investors remained cautious due to high oil prices, which are currently at $115 per barrel. However, a notable surge in smallcap stocks is enhancing investor confidence. Analysts attribute this positive momentum to better corporate fundamentals and increased domestic fund inflows.

items.title: Aerospace stock Aequs plunges 19% after Q2 results. Why are investors worried?
items.description: Aequs shares fell sharply on Tuesday after the aerospace manufacturer’s Q2 FY27 net loss more than doubled to Rs 52 crore. Revenue rose 45% year-on-year, but EBITDA fell 45% and margins narrowed. Brokerages flagged weakness in the consumer business and delayed breakeven expectations, even as the aerospace order book remained strong.

items.title: India’s ₹1 lakh crore club stocks hit hard by FII exit. Have bluechips lost their growth engines?
items.description: India's largest corporations are experiencing a notable drop in foreign institutional investor stakes, raising concerns about their growth trajectory. This trend has adversely affected numerous large-cap stocks over recent months. Analysts suggest a shift in focus towards emerging sectors is critical for revitalizing foreign investments, as many companies now appear more like consistent cash flow generators than true growth catalysts.

items.title: Q2 earnings done for HDFC Bank, ICICI, other private lenders. What's next?
items.description: Private banks delivered mixed Q2 FY27 earnings, prompting analysts to identify lenders with attractive valuations and flag those investors may want to avoid. HDFC Bank reported a 5% YoY rise in net profit to Rs 19,510 crore, largely in line with expectations, but its shares have fallen 6% since the results.

items.title: Paytm shares rise 2% after Q2 results. What are Jefferies, Goldman Sachs, and others saying?
items.description: Paytm shares rose after the fintech major reported a 976% year-on-year jump in Q2 net profit and 28% revenue growth. Jefferies, Goldman Sachs and Citi retained Buy ratings, with target prices pointing to potential upside.

items.title: Tata Consumer shares rally over 4% after Q2 results. Why brokerages remain bullish despite target price cuts
items.description: Tata Consumer Products reported 16% year-on-year profit growth in Q2FY27, while brokerages retained positive ratings but cut target prices amid inflationary pressures. Jefferies, Nuvama, Elara Capital and Systematix see varying upside potential in the stock.

items.title: HAL, BEL, Paras Defence, other stocks rise up to 4% after DAC clears  proposals worth Rs 2.12 lakh crore
items.description: India’s Defence Acquisition Council approved defence procurement proposals worth Rs 2.12 lakh crore, with 82% expected from domestic industry. The clearances cover helicopters, drones, air-defence systems, artillery and naval platforms, supporting military modernisation. Defence stocks may gain investor attention, while indigenous manufacturing, rising capital expenditure and policy support strengthen long-term sector growth prospects.

items.title: MTAR Technologies among 4 stocks closing above VWAP
items.description: On October 26, four Nifty500 stocks closed more than 2.5% above their respective volume-weighted average prices (VWAPs), according to StockEdge’s technical scan data. VWAP measures a stock’s average traded price weighted by volume, giving greater importance to prices at which higher trading volumes occurred. A closing price above VWAP indicates that the stock ended the session above its volume-weighted average traded price.

items.title: JSW Steel among 5 stocks showing the White Marubozu pattern
items.description: On October 26, five Nifty500 stocks that gained over 4% appeared in StockEdge’s White Marubozu bullish scanner. A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in which the opening price is the lowest and the closing price is the highest during a given period.The pattern appears as a long white or green candlestick with no upper shadow and little or no lower shadow. It reflects strong buying pressure during the session and is commonly used in technical analysis to assess price momentum.

items.title: Ather Energy among 5 stocks showing RSI trending up
items.description: On October 26, five Nifty500 stocks that gained over 5% appeared in the RSI Trending Up scan, according to StockEdge data. The signal occurs when a stock’s Relative Strength Index (RSI) crosses above 50 from below. An upward-trending RSI indicates strengthening momentum in the stock’s price. The RSI is a technical indicator traders use to assess price momentum and trend strength.

items.title: Market wrap: Bharti Airtel, Tata Consumer, Asian Paints, Coal India top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Tuesday
items.description: Indian equity benchmarks ended nearly flat on Tuesday, with the Nifty 50 slipping 0.02% and the Sensex falling 8 points amid elevated crude prices and caution ahead of the US Fed decision. Tata Consumer and Bharti Airtel led gainers, while Asian Paints and Coal India topped the losers’ list.

items.title: UPI-MDR an additional earnings opportunity, not Paytm's business model foundation: Brokerages
items.description: Paytm has reported a substantial increase in revenue, demonstrating the success of its existing business model. The company's EBITDA has improved due to efficient cost control and a strong merchant franchise. Financial services have significantly contributed to revenue growth, highlighting the diversity of its business operations. Global brokerages support the view that UPI-MDR will enhance, rather than define, future profitability.

items.title: 10 microcap stocks rally up to 80% in just 3 months
items.description: Over the past three months, both the benchmark Nifty 50 and the Nifty Microcap 250 index have declined by around 4%. However, bucking the broader market trend, 40 stocks in the Nifty Microcap 250 index delivered double-digit price gains during the same period. Among these outperformers, we highlight the top 10 stocks that surged between 30% and 80% in just three months. (Data Source: ACE Equity)

items.title: Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders shares crash 10% after Q2 net profit tumbles 54%; firm declares Rs 5/share dividend
items.description: Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders shares plunged 10% after the state-owned company reported a 54% year-on-year decline in Q2 FY27 net profit to Rs 344 crore. Revenue from operations fell 16.5% to Rs 2,446 crore, while margins contracted sharply. The company also declared an interim dividend of Rs 5 per share.

items.title: Indian lenders defer dollar debt sale plan as rates turn expensive
items.description: Amidst rising US Treasury yields and a depreciating rupee, multiple Indian banks, such as Canara Bank, PNB, and Bank of India, are delaying their dollar debt initiatives. The looming expiration of the Reserve Bank of India’s hedging facility in December adds further pressure to these institutions. Nevertheless, there remains a glimmer of optimism among certain banks regarding potential future dollar bond sales as market conditions evolve.

items.title: Forget short-term pressure; in the long term, the right business is what pays: 5 mid-cap stocks with an upside potential of up to 36%
items.description: We have said this before, and we say it again: No one can predict when the market will bottom out. You can see the bottom only in hindsight, once it has been reached. So, don’t try to catch the bottom; try, instead, to own the right business.

items.title: D-Street in gloomy mood, but Kotak sees 3 triggers for rebounds and adds 5 midcap stocks to portfolio
items.description: Dalal Street faces significant market challenges, leading Kotak Institutional Equities to spotlight selective stock value. With large-cap stocks in view, the impact of geopolitical strife and fluctuating crude oil prices weighs heavily on investor sentiment. The brokerage sees potential recovery catalysts in peace talks regarding the Iran-US situation and favorable Q2 earnings.

items.title: Diwali stock picks! Axis picks Eternal, Hindalco, 7 other stocks with upside potential of up to 20%. See full list
items.description: Samvat 2082 proved challenging for Indian equities, marked by heightened volatility, intermittent recoveries and a significant correction in benchmark indices. Over the next 12 months, the sustainability and breadth of corporate earnings growth are likely to be the key drivers of equity market returns. Here are 9 stocks Axis Direct is bullish on this Diwali.

items.title: Mankind Pharma shares jump 8% as Q2 profit rises 38% to Rs 716 crore
items.description: Mankind Pharma shares jumped nearly 8% after the company reported a 38% year-on-year rise in Q2 profit to Rs 716 crore. Revenue grew 17%, supported by domestic and export growth, while EBITDA margins expanded 210 basis points.

items.title: Jio’s big-bang listing may give it stock market’s No.2 crown after Reliance Industries
items.description: Jio Platforms could overtake Bharti Airtel to become India’s second-largest listed company after its October 28 debut, with a 22% grey market premium implying a market capitalisation of Rs 12.5 lakh crore. Its Rs 30,213-crore IPO drew 22.2 times subscription, while brokerages highlighted growth opportunities in broadband, enterprise technology and AI.

items.title: Jefferies says Vodafone Idea shares can soar 143% in bull case scenario. 3 reasons why brokerage is upbeat
items.description: Jefferies sees a wide risk-reward range for Vodafone Idea, forecasting up to 143% upside in its bull case and 25% downside in its bear case. Network expansion, improving subscriber trends and tariff hikes could support strong revenue and EBITDA growth.

items.title: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Wednesday
items.description: Sensex and Nifty closed marginally lower as elevated crude oil prices and Fed uncertainty tempered sentiment. Smallcaps surged over 2%, midcaps gained over 1%, and market breadth favoured bulls, with 2,455 NSE stocks advancing.

items.title: US Fed opens two-day meeting with markets expecting rate hold
items.description: Policymakers at the US Federal Reserve opened a two-day meeting Tuesday to set interest rates, with markets expecting them to hold steady days ahead of crucial midterm elections. On Tuesday, markets put the probability of rates being held steady at near 90 percent, as per CME's FedWatch tool. aha/mjf

items.title: PVR Inox among stocks that hit 52-week highs and rallied up to 20% in a month
items.description: On Tuesday, the benchmark Sensex ended nearly flat, slipping 8 points to close at 73,598. Despite the subdued market sentiment, six stocks from the BSE 500 index touched fresh 52-week highs, marking their highest price levels in the past year. A 52-week high represents the highest price at which a stock has traded over the preceding 12 months and can indicate increased market activity and investor interest.

items.title: Two Trades for Today: A defence tech company for a 9.4% gain, a large-cap auto components stock for an upmove of about 7%
items.description: Our technical analysts identify select stocks every trading day that may gain momentum even in volatile markets. Here are the technical calls for today.

items.title: Sebi extends deadline for debenture trustees to comply with norms till April 2027
items.description: Sebi has extended the deadline for debenture trustees to comply with regulatory requirements by six months. The new deadline for compliance is now set for April 27, 2027. This extension was granted after receiving industry feedback about operational challenges faced by debenture trustees. The regulator is currently reviewing the regulatory framework related to debenture trustees through an Expert Working Group.
